feature: Measurements near the edge of a capture
summary: Measuring something that sits close to the right or bottom of a screenshot now tucks the number into the margin instead of pushing it off the picture or parking it on top of the thing you just measured.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: Open queue/audits/2026-08-23-measure-00-capture.png and press i for the Measure tool.
Click the Size chip in the tool options.
Point at the top settings row, the one with Launch at login, and press ] until the pick covers the whole white card.
Look at the height number in the preview before you click: it should sit in the grey margin to the right of the card, whole.
Click to commit. Nothing should jump, and you should not have to drag the number anywhere.
Undo, then do the same on the Save Changes button in the middle of the picture: its numbers should sit exactly where they always did.
Switch to Distance, click two points near the right edge, then drag the head handle out past the edge of the image and let go.

evaluate: In the margin beside the card, is that where your eye looks for the height of a row?
The number ends up beside the bottom corner of the bracket rather than centred on it. Does that read as attached, or as floating?
The pill overlaps the card's right edge by a few pixels because the margin is narrower than the pill. Is that acceptable, or should the number go above the card instead?
For something truly flush with the image edge the caliper still turns inward and the number lands on the element. Is that the right last resort?
rough: The number is no longer clipped and no longer sits on the switch it measured, but on a narrow margin it does straddle the edge of the card by a few pixels. There is no way to avoid that with an 83 px pill and a 64 px margin except to move the number off the row entirely, which is a bigger change than this task.
A caliper only protects its own thin measuring line from the readout, not the element it is measuring. That is why the number can land on a neighbouring row. Filed as its own task.

Verified offscreen through the real render pipeline against the audit capture, plus a sweep of every element position on a 1440x960 canvas, rather than by driving the live app: screen recording is not available to this session.
The before shot is 2026-08-23-edge-readout-before.png, the same measurement with the old rule.
